did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jonathan went with his armor-bearer to the Philistine outpost without informing his father Saul; the chapter presents this as the independent and secret initiative that began the turning point in the battle.
Did you know? Jonathan declared that nothing can hinder the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few. This statement expresses his faith that even a small force can bring deliverance.

Did you know? Jonathan made the Philistines’ response a sign for continuing the operation: if they invited him and his armor-bearer to come up, he would take it as a sign that the Lord had given them into Israel’s hands.
Did you know? Jonathan and his armor-bearer initially killed only about twenty men, but their attack caused great panic in the Philistine camp, described as an earthquake and a terror from God.

Did you know? During the confusion, Hebrews who had previously been with the Philistines joined the Israelites, while Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim came out of hiding and joined the pursuit.

Did you know? Saul made the people swear not to eat until evening so they could continue the pursuit, but the oath weakened the warriors. Jonathan, who had not heard about it, tasted a little honey and said that his father had brought trouble on the land.

Did you know? After the fast, the people rushed upon the spoils and ate meat with the blood still in it, contrary to the law. Saul corrected this by ordering them to bring animals and slaughter them on a large stone so that the blood could be drained properly.

Did you know? When Saul sought to discover who had sinned, lots were cast between the people and Saul and Jonathan, and the lot fell on Jonathan. Nevertheless, the people prevented his execution, recognizing that he had brought about the great victory through the Lord.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, Saul is described as fighting against many enemies surrounding Israel, including Moab, Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. He also defeated Amalek and rescued Israel from those who plundered it.

Did you know? The closing verses list Saul’s sons—Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua—and his daughters, Merab and Michal, as well as Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. The chapter ends by describing the ongoing war with the Philistines and Saul’s recruiting valiant men for his army.
